I have been farming this land in Quzhou my whole life. My father grew wheat and corn here, and his father before him. I know this soil, I know what grows, and I know what the traders in town will buy. I am 59 now — my back is not what it was — so I do not want to try anything new or risky. I have about 9 mu of contracted land. I will do the same rotation I always do: winter wheat, then summer corn on the same ground. That is two crops a year, same as every family around here.

For the wheat I will use the improved variety from the village cooperative — I have used it for years and it does not give me trouble. I put down compound fertilizer before plowing, then add urea when the wheat is jointing. I irrigate four times: once before sowing to wet the ground, once before winter freeze, once at jointing, once at heading. I spray for weeds in autumn and then spray once more if I see powdery mildew or aphids in spring.

For the corn I will buy hybrid seed from the county seed shop, same brand as last year. I seed it straight into the wheat stubble right after harvest — no point tilling again in that heat, and my neighbor's machine does it for me cheap. Corn gets more urea split into two top-dressings. Summer rains help but I still irrigate twice when it gets dry. I spray for fall armyworm because it has been bad the last few years.

I do not expect to get rich. I expect a stable harvest I can sell and keep enough to eat.
